verification.summary: HERCULES STAR, a Gibraltar flagged oil products tanker of 7,998 deadweight, was struck by an unknown projectile in the early hours of 9 September 2026 while at anchor off Dubai, about 24 nautical miles northwest of Port Rashid. The Russian Consulate General in Dubai told REN TV that the body of a Russian seafarer missing after the damage to the tanker had been found and would be repatriated, and the Philippine Department of Migrant Workers repatriated the remains of a Filipino seafarer killed in the same incident. The IMO confirmed incident register records the ship damaged, no pollution and two seafarer fatalities on 9 September. The same tanker had been hit earlier, on 1 March 2026 near Mina Saqr, causing a fire with no injuries; that is a separate attack.
verification.date_note: Peninsula's statements and the IMO register both date this attack to 9 September 2026, and the Philippine repatriation notice names 9 September at the Dubai Delta anchorage. verification.location_text: About 11 nautical miles north of Oman
verification.summary: MAYUREE NAREE, a Thai-flagged bulk carrier owned by Precious Shipping, was struck by two projectiles of unknown origin about 11 nautical miles north of Oman on 11 March 2026 while in ballast from Khalifa Port towards India. The projectiles hit above the waterline, set the engine room on fire and left it flooded. Twenty of the 23 Thai crew were taken off with help from the Omani navy and flew home on 16 March, and three were trapped in the engine room. A search team hired by Precious Shipping found human remains in the damaged area, as Thailand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported on 3 April 2026, and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow confirmed on 8 April that all three had died. Their remains were repatriated to Thailand in early July.
verification.date_note: The strike was reported on 11 March in Gulf local time, which is UTC+4, so the UTC date is also 11 March; no exact event time was published.

verification.location_text: 6NM north of Oman
verification.summary: MUSSAFAH 2, an Emirati flagged salvage tug operated by Abu Dhabi Ports, was hit by two missiles at about 02:00 local time on 6 March 2026 while preparing to tow the abandoned container ship SAFEEN PRESTIGE, which had been struck two days earlier. UKMTO reported an incident six nautical miles north of Oman in which a tug was hit by unknown projectiles, and the IMO confirmed incident register records four seafarer fatalities and three severely injured on this ship that day. The tug caught fire and sank. Indonesia's foreign ministry said the tug had seven crew from Indonesia, India and the Philippines, that four survived and that three Indonesians were missing. The Migrant Workers Office of the Philippine Embassy in Abu Dhabi said the second missile hit the bridge, where four crew including the only Filipino on board were standing, and that all four were missing and presumed dead.
verification.date_note: UKMTO 015-26, the IMO register and the owner linked reporting all give the attack as 6 March 2026. Initial reports spoke of eight crew aboard while Indonesia's foreign ministry gave seven, and about thirteen people were on the tug and the container ship together, so the crew total is recorded as reported rather than reconciled. The Indonesian ministry's toll of four survivors and three missing sits beside the IMO toll of four dead and three severely injured; the two are kept side by side and not merged.

updates.text: Authority sourced narrative added to a record that rested on the IMO register row alone. UKMTO warning 015-26, carried in Joint Maritime Information Center advisory update 081, names MUSSAFAH 2 as a tug struck by projectiles on 6 March 2026 while supporting operations with the container ship SAFEEN PRESTIGE. The register keeps four seafarer fatalities and three severely injured, and the injured snapshot is now dated to the attack rather than to the register check. The sinking and the crew breakdown are taken from Agence France-Presse quoting Indonesia's foreign ministry, which reported seven crew from Indonesia, India and the Philippines and three Indonesians missing. No nationality is recorded for the four deaths because no source assigns one, and the missing three are not counted as dead.

updates.text: Crew nationalities added to a record that carried four deaths with no nationality detail. The IMO register confirms four seafarer fatalities and three severely injured on this tug. Indonesia's foreign ministry named three Indonesian crew members, including the captain, as missing, and the Philippine Embassy's Migrant Workers Office in Abu Dhabi reported that the second missile struck the bridge where four crew including the only Filipino on board were standing and that all four were missing and presumed dead. On that basis the four deaths are recorded as three Indonesian and one Filipino: the four men reported missing are the four fatalities in the IMO total. The two authorities disagree on the structure of the toll, the ministry giving four survivors and three missing while the IMO gives four dead and three severely injured, and that conflict is left visible rather than averaged. updates.text: Casualty count settled and the Indonesian missing snapshot cleared. Yemen's transport ministry, reported by BBC News and Al Jazeera on 12 August 2026, states that three ballistic missiles hit Tihamah south of Mocha on 11 August and that four crew were killed: three Pakistani nationals and one Indonesian national. This replaces the earlier minimum of two Pakistani deaths and clears the minimum flag. The ministry's one Indonesian dead is the seafarer the Indonesian foreign ministry briefing of 13 August carried as missing, since the other two Indonesian crew were reported safe at that briefing; the missing snapshot of one is therefore dropped rather than added to the dead, so nothing is double counted; the previous snapshot remains in the audit history. The six dead reported overall include at least two troops killed when a second missile struck the rescue party; those are not seafarer deaths and are not added to the crew total. The injured snapshot of eight is preserved unchanged because the coastguard's ten wounded in total, including seven crew, conflicts with the eight injured survivors reported earlier by Pakistan's deputy prime minister, and no settled injured figure is asserted here. Vessel identity, IMO 1031329, the Tanzanian flag and the 11 August date are unchanged.

verification.location_text: About 70NM east of Byala, inside Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone
verification.summary: ABLE, a Palau flagged general cargo ship of 7,416 deadweight built in 1991 and Turkish owned, was attacked by air and sea drones about 70 nautical miles east of Byala, inside Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, in the early hours of 6 October 2026 while carrying barley from Romania to Turkey. A fire broke out and the engine room began to fill with water. Bulgaria's Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the ferry Dioscuria, the navy and the border police rescued all 18 crew, 11 Turkish and 7 Indian; two were injured in the fire and taken to Varna for treatment. The ship stayed afloat, left the Bulgarian zone on 14 October and, according to Nova Televizia as reported by Sofia Globe, disappeared from radar late on 19 October and sank off the Turkish coast.
verification.date_note: Bulgarian officials placed the attack at about 03:00 local time on 6 October 2026; the BBC gives 23:00 GMT. The record keeps 6 October, the date used by the Bulgarian government and by the Bulgarian and international reporting checked.

It now rests on the Bulgarian government account reported by the BBC and The Maritime Executive: drones hit the Palau flagged general cargo ship Able about 70NM east of Byala on 6 October 2026, starting a fire and flooding the engine room, and all 18 crew, 11 Turkish and 7 Indian, were rescued, two of them injured and taken to Varna. The injured snapshot of two is dated 6 October 2026. Deaths stay zero for this ship: nobody on the Able is reported dead. The crew of the Alfa Watan, the other ship attacked in the same incident, are recorded under that ship and are not counted here. verification.summary: HS Dignity, a Guinea-Bissau-flagged general cargo ship with 16 people aboard, was struck by a drone at about 01:20 local time on 13 October 2026 and sank 17 nautical miles east of Shabla, Bulgaria, while in ballast from Mostaganem in Algeria towards Braila in Romania. Survivors were taken aboard AZOV CONCORD and the Danish-flagged SCANDI ASSERTER. Bulgaria's Ministry of Transport and Communications declared the search and rescue operation over at 15:00 on 14 October, and the ministry's closing statement as carried by the Bulgarian News Agency records six crew members rescued and 10 unaccounted for. No body has been recovered and no authority has published a death for this sinking.

updates.text: First reviewed living record for this sinking. Bulgaria's Ministry of Transport and Communications reported six crew rescued and 10 unaccounted for when the search ended on 14 October; Bulgarian outlets and the Syrian Sailors Union reported five rescued and 11 missing, and 24 Chasa said the fifth survivor reached Varna later on another ship. Because the rescued and missing split is unresolved, no missing figure is recorded as a snapshot and no death is counted. The ministry places the sinking 17 nautical miles east of Shabla; some reports say 15 to 17 miles east of Krapets. No nationality is recorded for the missing: Syria's Foreign Ministry told SANA on 18 October that 14 Syrians and two Egyptians were aboard, while other accounts gave 12 Syrians, and crew nationality is not inferred from the flag.

sources.source: Bulgarian News Agency (BTA), 14 October 2026

updates.text: CBC News reported on 24 October 2026 that five of the 16 crew survived and that 11 remained officially listed as missing, and that the crew was made up of Syrian and Egyptian nationals. That matches the five rescued and 11 missing reported by Bulgarian outlets, while Bulgaria's Ministry of Transport and Communications said six were rescued and 10 were unaccounted for when the search ended on 14 October. The difference is not resolved, so 11 missing is recorded as a dated snapshot and no death is counted. No nationality is assigned to the missing because neither source gives a breakdown of the crew by nationality.

updates.text: Casualty follow-up, death count still unresolved. CNN reported on 3 November 2026 that 11 of the crew on the HS Dignity, most of them Syrian, died. The Egyptian maritime officers syndicate said on 15 October that the search had ended with five rescued, among them the Egyptian chief officer Ashraf Mamdouh and four Syrian seafarers, and that the 11 unaccounted for, including the Egyptian master Mustafa El-Sayed Hegazi El-Ghazi, were to be treated as deceased; it said formal proof of death still required a cabinet decision published in the Official Gazette. The Bulgarian Ministry of Transport and Communications closed its search on 14 October with six rescued and ten unaccounted for, while the Syrian Sailors Union and the Egyptian syndicate give five rescued and 11 missing from a crew of 16, 14 Syrian and two Egyptian. The syndicate statement gives a total of 11 but then names the Egyptian master and 11 Syrian seafarers, so its breakdown is not used. The small boat attached two explosive devices to the hull above the waterline and the blasts caused a fire in the engine room that temporarily disabled the ship. UKMTO reported on 30 October that a verified report confirmed the crew were safe, that there was no environmental impact, that the fire was extinguished and that the vessel was continuing to its next port of call. Maritime security firm Vanguard Tech, cited by Seatrade Maritime, identified the ship as the Panama-flagged Louise 1 of 159,092 deadweight tonnes, owned by Panama-based Aquarius Maritime Ventures, and those particulars match the crude oil tanker IMO 9290323. Iran's army navy said a tanker had struck a naval mine in a restricted area east of the strait, which contradicts the UKMTO account. India's minister for ports, shipping and waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, said in a post on 30 October 2026 that 27 Indian seafarers were aboard LOUISE 1 and that all 29 Indian seafarers on the two tankers struck on 29 and 30 October were completely safe with no injuries. Reuters, cited by The Times of India and India Today, reported that three maritime security sources said two limpet mines had been attached to the hull by a small craft.
verification.date_note: UKMTO warning 187-26 gives the attack as 29 October 2026 at 2212 UTC. The crew-safe update was issued at 0150 UTC on 30 October, which is why some reports carry a 30 October date.

updates.text: Follow-up on the review of 1 November 2026. Two sourced facts are added and the casualty count does not change. UKMTO warning 188-26, as listed in JMIC advisory update 110 issued on 1 November, gives the position as about 40 nautical miles south of Lavan Island, Iran, records projectiles as the cause, states that a fire broke out on board and reports the crew as safe. The earlier review had recorded that no position and no damage detail had been published beyond the owner's assessment; that is no longer true, so the location is filled in and the attack type now follows the UKMTO wording of projectiles rather than the owner's unidentified objects. TradeWinds reported on 2 November that QatarEnergy was weighing options for offloading cargo from the damaged carrier and described a port-side strike, which is consistent with the UKMTO fire report and shows damage beyond the owner's safe and operational line, although no authority has published a damage assessment. Deaths stay at zero on the owner's statement that no one on board was injured and on UKMTO reporting the crew as safe, not on silence, and no nationality is entered because no casualty is reported.

updates.text: Correction to a merge, not to the casualty count. The 2 November 2026 report held as INC-20261102-012 and merged into this row is not about AL MAYEDA. AL MAYEDA was struck about 40 nautical miles south of Lavan Island on 30 October 2026 and its owner Nakilat stated that none of the crew on board were injured, so this row's confirmed position of no deaths and no injuries is unchanged. The merged 2 November report must not be read as an AL MAYEDA casualty, and its single death must not be counted twice.

update.text: First sourced identity and casualty check for this record, which until now carried only aggregated headlines. The tanker is confirmed as PETRO DOLPHIN, IMO 1072294, a Nicaragua-flagged products tanker of about 4,000 dwt, struck by a UAV at Sohar Anchorage in the Gulf of Oman on 11 October 2026 and evacuated. UKMTO warning 165-26 and the JMIC advisory of 15 October confirm the weapon and the evacuation, and the IMO register confirms the name, IMO number, date and place with two seafarers missing. India's shipping minister said 11 Indian seafarers were aboard, nine rescued, and two Indian nationals missing; the External Affairs Ministry gave the crew as 12, of whom nine Indians and one Bangladeshi were rescued, and the seafarers union named the two missing men. No authority has reported a death, and the crew video and family statements reported in the press are not a death confirmation, so the death count stays unknown rather than zero and the two missing are recorded as a dated missing snapshot only. Both missing men are Indian nationals on the statement of India's shipping minister, but the nationality list stays empty because no death has been confirmed to attach a nationality to. The crew nationalities come from the Indian government and ministry statements, not from the Nicaraguan flag. The record previously merged a UKMTO report of an unnamed tanker struck in the Strait of Hormuz on the same day into this attack; those were separate strikes on 11 October recorded elsewhere in the tracker as UKMTO warnings 166-26 to 169-26, and the region here is corrected to the Gulf of Oman, outside the strait, per the UKMTO position and the IMO entry. No image is published.

update.text: Follow-up on a record first reviewed on 26 October. Three things are added and the count does not change. India's Ministry of External Affairs said the two seafarers killed were foreign nationals, so neither death was Indian, and that all three Indian crew members were safe with one of them injured; that is the first authority statement ruling out an Indian fatality here and it is why no Indian nationality entry exists. Azerbaijan's maritime outlet SeaNews reported on 6 October that the two Azerbaijani crew who died were the captain, Rustam Hasanov, and the cook, Mahammad Suleymanzade, the man Azerbaijan's foreign ministry had listed as missing on the same day; JamNews, publishing on 27 October, said there was still no further information about Suleymanzade's fate. Those two accounts conflict and neither is an owner, flag state or Romanian authority statement, so the second death keeps no attributed nationality and the Azerbaijani nationality count stays at one. The Romanian tally of eleven survivors and two bodies accounts for all thirteen crew, which is why no missing snapshot is carried on this record and why the Azerbaijani crew member reported missing on 6 October is not listed as missing here; his disposition in public sources remains unresolved. Two deaths stand on the Romanian authority's recovery of two bodies, and nothing is inferred from silence. One further point on the injured: Azerbaijan's foreign ministry reported three Azerbaijani crew hospitalised, while India's Ministry of External Affairs said some crew including Indian nationals were injured and one of the three Indians needed medical attention; the two accounts cannot be reconciled into a single injured total from the sources read, so the injured snapshot stays at three and the Indian injury is recorded here rather than added to it.

verification.location_text: About 13 nautical miles east of Constanta, outside Romanian territorial waters, at 44 06.59 N 029 01.10 E
verification.summary: KHORYV, a Comoros-flagged ore/oil carrier of 3,280 dwt built in 1983, was 13 nautical miles off Constanta en route from Eregli to Sulina when it sent a distress signal at about 10:00 local time on 23 October 2026 and caught fire. Romania's Naval Authority said the 13 crew were 10 Ukrainian and 3 Azerbaijani nationals, that intervention vessels recovered nine people alive and one body from the water, and that three crew were still missing while the search continued in poor weather. The ship capsized and lay upside down, and Romanian hydrographic warning ARN 153/2026 gave its position as 44 06.59 N 029 01.10 E. Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the dead seafarer was a Ukrainian citizen, that four Ukrainians including the master were taken to hospital, that two Ukrainians needed no medical treatment and that the three crew still missing are Ukrainian. Azerbaijan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said all three Azerbaijani crew were rescued and that one of them had minor injuries, was examined and was accommodated in a hotel. Romania's president, Nicusor Dan, said the vessel had been struck by a drone; the naval authority's statement did not establish the cause.
verification.date_note: Romanian local time on 23 October is UTC+3, so the 10:00 distress call was about 07:00 UTC on the same day. The day-precision UTC date is kept as reported. Ukraine's ministry put the crew at 14 while Romania's naval authority reported 13; the difference stays recorded and unresolved.

updates.text: Follow-up on a record reviewed on 25 October. Two sourced facts are added and neither changes the casualty count. Romanian rescuers suspended the search for the three missing crew at 18:04 on 24 October because of poor visibility, after almost four hours of work by the rescue vessel SAR Artemis and a Black Hawk helicopter of the General Aviation Inspectorate, and it was not known on 25 October whether the search had resumed. Separately, Romania's Maritime Hydrographic Directorate published warning ARN 155/2026 on 25 October, cancelling ARN 154/2026, and reported M/V KHORYV at 43 55.25 N 028 57.40 E at 09:00 UTC that day, still afloat and capsized, with three crew members reported missing and a one nautical mile keep clear because the hull is a danger to navigation. That notice is the same Comoros flagged ore and oil carrier sunk on 23 October. It is a wreck position update, not a second attack, not a completed sinking and not a closed search. One death stays confirmed and flagged as a minimum, the three missing men stay a dated missing snapshot and are not counted as dead, and the suspension of the search does not change their status.

verification.summary: AL MAYEDA, an LNG carrier owned by Qatar Gas Transport Company (Nakilat) and flagged in the Marshall Islands, was hit by unidentified objects while transiting the Arabian Gulf on the evening of Friday 30 October 2026. Nakilat's statement, published on the Qatar Stock Exchange and carried by the Qatar News Agency on 1 November, said none of the crew members on board were injured, there was no impact on the environment, the vessel was in a safe condition and operational, and the impact of the incident was being assessed. India's shipping minister, Sarbananda Sonowal, said in a post on X on 31 October that the Marshall Islands-flagged LNG carrier MT AL MAYEDA, carrying six Indian seafarers, was targeted in a projectile attack in the Persian Gulf on 30 October, and that all six Indian nationals along with the entire 25-member crew were completely safe. No position, attacker or damage detail beyond the owner's assessment has been published, and the owner named no weapon.
verification.date_note: Nakilat's statement, carried by the Qatar News Agency, dates the strike to the evening of Friday 30 October 2026, and India's shipping minister also gives 30 October. The corpus row and the first reports carry 1 November, the day the owner's statement was published, so the attack date is recorded as 30 October.

update.text: Correction to this row's date and identity, no new attack. The Turkish shipping outlet Denizhaber published on 4 November 2026 a report headed that a seafarer had died in a drone attack on a commercial ship in the Black Sea, and its own text shows the report describes the attack of 3 October 2026: it cites TradeWinds of 4 October, the Ukrainian Sea Ports Authority statement of 3 October and Reuters of 3 October, and sets out a Liberian flagged bulker off Chornomorsk in which one crew member died, three were injured and 13 were evacuated. Reuters reported on 3 October that the Ukrainian sea ports administration said Russia attacked a Liberian flagged cargo ship in one of Ukraine's Black Sea ports in the Odesa region, killing one person and injuring three, with 13 other crew members evacuated. That event is already held in this archive as INC-20261003-001, so the 4 November headline adds no new attack and no new death and must not be counted as a separate casualty. Separately, Russia's defence ministry claimed on 4 November that it had struck a dry cargo vessel about 8 kilometres south west of Odesa overnight, as carried by UNN, which states there is no independent confirmation; no authority has reported a casualty for that claim, so it is held here only as an unconfirmed claim and no count is attached to it. Odesa's regional military administration reported overnight strikes into 4 November on an energy facility, a shopping centre and a residential area, and its head Oleh Kiper said there were no casualties, according to Ukrainska Pravda. No vessel is named anywhere in the checked reporting for 4 November and no nationality is recorded.

verification.summary: HS Dignity, a Guinea-Bissau-flagged general cargo ship with 16 people aboard, was struck by a drone at about 01:20 local time on 13 October and sank 17 nautical miles east of Shabla, Bulgaria. Four survivors were taken aboard AZOV CONCORD and a fifth by the Danish-flagged SCANDI ASSERTER; Bulgaria's Ministry of Transport and Communications declared the search and rescue operation over at 15:00 on 14 October.
verification.date_note: Local Bulgarian time is UTC+3, so 01:20 on 13 October falls at 22:20 UTC on 12 October; the ministry and the Bulgarian News Agency date the sinking 13 October and the day-precision UTC date is kept as reported, not recalculated.

updates.text: First reviewed living record for this sinking. Bulgaria's Ministry of Transport and Communications reported six crew rescued and 10 unaccounted for when the search ended on 14 October; Bulgarian outlets and the Syrian Sailors Union reported five rescued and 11 missing, and 24 Chasa said the fifth survivor reached Varna later on another ship. Because the rescued and missing split is unresolved, no missing figure is recorded as a snapshot and no death is counted. The ministry places the sinking 17 nautical miles east of Shabla; some reports say 15 to 17 miles east of Krapets.
